name: Infix/Postfix/Prefix Expression Conversion & Evaluation
recognitionClueHinglish: Ek arithmetic expression di hai (infix ya postfix form me) aur poocha hai equivalent postfix/prefix form kya hai, ya postfix expression ka VALUE evaluate karna hai — ye classic stack-application pattern hai.
whatShouldComeToMind: Infix→Postfix: use an operator stack, respect precedence+associativity, pop higher-or-equal precedence operators before pushing new ones.
Postfix evaluation: push operands, on operator pop TWO, apply, push result back — watch operand ORDER for non-commutative operators.
generalSolvingApproach: 1. For conversion: scan infix left to right; operand → output directly; operator → pop stack while top has higher-or-equal precedence (respecting associativity), then push; at end pop all remaining.
2. For evaluation: scan postfix left to right; operand → push; operator → pop two (second-popped is LEFT operand for non-commutative ops), compute, push result.
3. Double check operand order for '-' and '/' specifically — easy to swap.
variationsObserved: Expression includes exponentiation (right-associative, different rule from left-associative +,-,*,/).
commonTraps: Swapping operand order for non-commutative operators during postfix evaluation.
Forgetting right-associativity of ^ during infix-to-postfix conversion.

name: Push/Pop Sequence Simulation (given operations or code, trace the result)
recognitionClueHinglish: Ek sequence of PUSH/POP operations di hai (ya C code jo stack implement karta hai), aur poocha hai final output/popped-values/sum kya hoga — is topic ka sabse bada pattern hai (19 me se 8 PYQs).
whatShouldComeToMind: Maintain an EXPLICIT stack list on paper/mentally, process every operation literally in the given order.
For code-based stack (array + top-pointer), track the array contents AND the top-pointer value together.
generalSolvingApproach: 1. Draw the stack as a vertical list, empty at start.
2. Process each operation (push/pop, or the equivalent code logic) one at a time, updating the drawn stack.
3. Record whatever is asked (popped sequence, final sum, final stack contents) as you go — don't try to compute it at the end from memory.
variationsObserved: Two stacks (or a stack and a queue) interacting simultaneously — track both structures in parallel.
Stack operations embedded in a while-loop with conditional logic (not a flat operation list) — trace the loop iteration by iteration.
commonTraps: Losing track of the stack's current state after several operations — always keep the explicit drawn stack updated, don't compute mentally.
edgeCases: Popping from an empty stack — check whether the question specifies this is guaranteed not to happen or needs special handling.

name: Valid Permutation / Achievable Output Sequence via Stack
recognitionClueHinglish: Input sequence di hai (jaise 1,2,3,4 order me push honge) aur poocha hai kaunsi OUTPUT sequences (permutations) stack push/pop se achievable hain — ye combinatorial-reasoning pattern hai.
whatShouldComeToMind: NOT every permutation is achievable — only Catalan-number-many are.
Fast check: does the candidate output sequence contain a '231 pattern' (some element popped between two others in the WRONG relative order)? If yes, impossible.
generalSolvingApproach: 1. For small n, just SIMULATE: try to produce the candidate output sequence using valid push/pop interleavings — if you get stuck (need to pop an element not yet pushed, or need to push out of order), it's invalid.
2. For a quick check without full simulation, look for the 231 forbidden pattern in the candidate sequence.
commonTraps: Assuming a 'reasonable-looking' permutation is automatically achievable without checking.

name: Stack Application / Conceptual (which DS to use, augmented operations)
recognitionClueHinglish: Poocha hai 'best data structure for X' (jaise balanced parentheses check), ya stack ko augment karke ek naya O(1) operation add karna hai (jaise MIN) — ye conceptual-application pattern hai.
whatShouldComeToMind: Balanced parentheses / nested-structure matching → Stack is the natural answer.
Augmenting stack with O(1) extra operations (like MIN/MAX) → maintain a SECOND auxiliary stack that tracks the running min/max alongside the main stack.
generalSolvingApproach: 1. For 'best DS' questions, match the problem's access pattern (nested/LIFO?) to the right structure.
2. For augmented-operation questions, think 'what extra bookkeeping, pushed/popped in sync with the main stack, would make this O(1)?' — usually a parallel auxiliary stack.
variationsObserved: Function f satisfying algebraic properties over stack states (f(push(S,x))=... ) — abstract but still solvable by tracing small concrete stacks.
commonTraps: Trying to achieve O(1) MIN/MAX by re-scanning the stack each time instead of using an auxiliary tracking stack.

name: Stack Implementation Design (two stacks in one array, queue-via-stack, REVERSE op)
recognitionClueHinglish: Poocha hai do stacks ko EK array me kaise efficiently fit karein, ya stack operations (PUSH/POP/REVERSE) use karke QUEUE kaise implement karein — ye design pattern hai.
whatShouldComeToMind: Two stacks in one array: grow from OPPOSITE ends toward the middle — much more space-efficient than a fixed 50/50 split.
Implementing Queue with Stack+REVERSE: ENQUEUE = push, then to DEQUEUE = reverse the stack then pop (or push-to-bottom trick) — think about which operation becomes expensive.
generalSolvingApproach: 1. For shared-array two-stack design: grow from opposite ends, only 'overflow' when the two tops meet in the middle — reason about worst-case space usage this way.
2. For queue-via-stack design questions: figure out which single stack operation (push, pop, or REVERSE) needs to be combined to emulate FIFO order, and how many operations that costs.
commonTraps: Assuming a fixed 50/50 array split is optimal for two stacks — opposite-ends growth is strictly better.
